title: Cambodia Confirms Resumption of Joint Military Exercises With US Next Year
gist: Cambodia's army has confirmed that Exercise Angkor Sentinel will resume with the United States in February 2027 after a decade-long suspension, the clearest sign yet of a US-Cambodia military thaw that also extends to Ream Naval Base.

themes.theme: Exercise resumption as a thaw marker

insights.claim: Cambodia's army has confirmed it will resume joint military exercises with the United States in early 2027 after a suspension lasting roughly a decade.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Strangio
insights.so_what: A decade-long freeze ending is a step-change in US-Cambodia relations and a partial offset to assumptions of exclusive Chinese influence in Phnom Penh.
insights.locator: Cambodia’s army has confirmed that it will resume joint military exercises

insights.claim: Officials from Cambodia and the United States concluded an Initial Planning Conference for Exercise Angkor Sentinel 2027, which the Royal Cambodian Army announced on Facebook and said would be held in February of next year.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Strangio
insights.so_what: A completed planning conference with a named month makes this a concrete calendar catalyst rather than an aspiration.
insights.locator: The Royal Cambodian Army announced on Facebook on Friday

insights.claim: The exercise resumption is presented as the latest in a series of signs that US-Cambodia ties are improving, implying a trend rather than a one-off gesture.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Strangio
insights.so_what: Treat further US-Cambodia defense engagement announcements as continuation of an established trajectory, not surprises.
insights.quote: the latest sign of the improving ties between the two nations
insights.locator: the latest sign of the improving ties

insights.claim: US Pacific Fleet commander Adm. Steve Koehler visited Cambodia's Ream Naval Base in Sihanoukville on August 7, 2026, alongside the US Charge d'Affaires and the Royal Cambodian Navy base commander.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Strangio
insights.so_what: US access to Ream — long viewed as a prospective Chinese facility — is the highest-stakes element of the thaw and the one to watch for follow-on port calls.
insights.locator: U.S. Navy Adm. Steve Koehler, commander of the U.S. Pacific Fleet
